question: In the derivation of Snell's law using Huygens' principle, we relate the angle of incidence ($i$) and the angle of refraction ($r$) to the velocities of light in the two media ($v_1$ and $v_2$). If light refracts from a rarer medium to a denser medium ($v_1 > v_2$), why must the angle of refraction $r$ be smaller than the angle of incidence $i$?

options.A: Because the secondary wavelets in the second medium travel a shorter distance in the same time interval, tilting the wavefront.
options.B: Because the frequency of the light increases in the denser medium, causing the wave to bend.
options.C: Because the amplitude of the wave decreases in the denser medium, shrinking the angle.
options.D: Because the secondary wavelets in the second medium travel faster, expanding the wavefront angle.
